import sys, json, re

# The incoming message and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects, beside
# `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is
# nothing to hand over). Every knob below is read from it, so each one is
# per-INSTANCE configuration -- two summarizers in one colony weight their days
# apart, and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a colony-wide
# environment. The literal beside each name is the shipped default; it is the
# same number the template config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins
# the three against each other.
_doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
P = _doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


# --- recency weighting (deterministic structure, no model judgement) --------
# How many of the newest turns travel VERBATIM into the prompt. Everything
# before them is the older part of the day, oldest first -- more from the last
# turns, phase-out before, hard facts kept (R-OS-3 handover).
RECENT_TURNS = _int("recent_turns", 12)
# How many tool-activity lines enter at most, newest kept; the dropped ones are
# named in the prompt, never lost in silence.
ROUND_LINES = _int("round_lines", 40)
# The window of `./writer` in tokens (GH #1085,
# R-IG-1): the catalog row of the model the writer is born on (OR-IG-9), named
# by `input_soft_fallback_row`: a birth token whose llm-registry tier is
# `light`, openai/gpt-6-luna -- 250000 tokens.
# 0: no window, the day travels whole.
INPUT_SOFT_FALLBACK = _int("input_soft_fallback", 250000)


# >>> content-budget v1 (R-IG-1, GH #1085)
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3


def budget_chars(input_soft, share):
    """Characters a producer may hand a model whose usable window is
    `input_soft` tokens (the catalog row, cut by the curator), for a section
    that takes `share` of that window. None when no window is known: the
    producer then delivers its content whole."""
    try:
        soft = int(float(input_soft))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if soft <= 0:
        return None
    return int(soft * share * CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def clip(text, limit, hint="budget of the window"):
    """`text` whole when it fits `limit` (None: no limit); else its head and
    a mark naming what was shown, the total and how to get the rest."""
    text = "" if text is None else str(text)
    if limit is None or len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    limit = max(0, int(limit))
    return text[:limit] + "...[cut: %d of %d chars shown; %s]" % (
        limit, len(text), hint)
# <<< content-budget v1


# R-IG-1 (GH #1085): no fixed length per turn or per tool text any more. Until
# summarizer 2.2.6 every older turn and every tool preview was cut to 200
# characters (`phaseout_chars`, `tool_chars`), whatever the window of the
# writer -- a handover built from fragments. Now the prompt takes HALF of the
# window of the model that READS it, `./writer` (the main content of a model
# call), never the window of the conversation the day came from: a context
# `input_soft` / `recall_input_soft` names the window of the model that ASKED,
# not of the writer (OR-IG-4), so prep reads neither. The writer's window is
# INPUT_SOFT_FALLBACK, the row of the model it is born on. A prompt the writer
# refuses as over its `input_hard` comes back on `in_error` and is sized ONCE
# more at half of the number the refusal names. No window: everything whole.
PROMPT_SHARE = 0.5
CUT_HINT = "budget of the window"


def asked_soft(ctx):
    """The writer's window (tokens): the fallback row of the model it is
    born on; None when it names none. `ctx` is not read on purpose."""
    if budget_chars(INPUT_SOFT_FALLBACK, 1.0) is not None:
        return INPUT_SOFT_FALLBACK
    return None


def _mark(shown, total):
    return "...[cut: %d of %d chars shown; %s]" % (shown, total, CUT_HINT)


def _mark_len(n):
    # The longest mark a text of n characters can carry.
    return len(_mark(n, n))


# A text that was cut once (a prompt the writer refused, read back) ends in its
# mark; cut again, it keeps naming the length it had before the FIRST cut.
CUT_TAIL = re.compile(r"\.\.\.\[cut: (\d+) of (\d+) chars shown; "
                      + re.escape(CUT_HINT) + r"\]$")


def item(lead, text):
    """One turn or tool text: what precedes it on its line, the text, and the
    length the text had before any cut."""
    m = CUT_TAIL.search(text)
    if m and int(m.group(1)) == m.start() and int(m.group(2)) > m.start():
        return {"lead": lead, "head": text[:m.start()], "total": int(m.group(2))}
    return {"lead": lead, "head": text, "total": len(text)}


def whole(it):
    if len(it["head"]) == it["total"]:
        return it["head"]
    return it["head"] + _mark(len(it["head"]), it["total"])


def fit(items, room):
    """The items' texts cut to share `room` characters fairly: every text that
    fits an equal share stays whole, the rest are cut to the same length, each
    with its mark (counted into the room). All of them whole when they fit."""
    texts = [whole(it) for it in items]
    lens = [len(t) for t in texts]
    if sum(lens) <= room:
        return texts
    cut, limit = set(), 0
    while True:
        left = max(0, room - sum(_mark_len(items[i]["total"]) for i in cut))
        order = sorted(range(len(lens)), key=lambda i: lens[i])
        limit = None
        for k, i in enumerate(order):
            share = left // (len(order) - k)
            if lens[i] <= share:
                left -= lens[i]
                continue
            limit = share
            break
        grown = {i for i, n in enumerate(lens) if limit is not None and n > limit}
        if grown <= cut:
            break
        cut |= grown
    out = []
    for i, it in enumerate(items):
        if i not in cut:
            out.append(texts[i])
            continue
        shown = min(max(0, int(limit)), len(it["head"]))
        out.append(it["head"][:shown] + _mark(shown, it["total"]))
    return out


# THE PROMPT DOCUMENT. A header, then up to three sections -- the older turns,
# the recent turns, the tool activity -- each a title and its entries: a turn
# or tool text (an item), or a fixed line (a `dropped` line, the empty-session
# line). One shape for the day a batch brings and for a refused prompt read
# back, so both are cut by the same rule.
TITLE_OLD = re.compile(r"^## \d+ older turns \(oldest first\)$")
TITLE_RECENT = "## Recent turns (verbatim, oldest first)"
TITLE_TOOLS = "## Tool activity (newest last)"
NO_TURNS = "(none - the session had no turns)"
TURN_LEAD = re.compile(r"^- (?:user|assistant): ")
TOOL_LEAD = re.compile(r"^- iter [^ ]* (?:call|result) [^:]*: ")


def render(header, sections, texts=None):
    lines = list(header)
    for n, sec in enumerate(sections):
        if n:
            lines.append("")
        lines.append(sec["title"])
        for e in sec["entries"]:
            if "line" in e:
                lines.append(e["line"])
            else:
                text = texts[id(e)] if texts is not None and id(e) in texts else whole(e)
                lines.append(e["lead"] + text)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def shape(header, sections, limit):
    """The prompt within `limit` characters (None: whole). The recent turns
    go first; the older turns and the tool texts share what is left, each cut
    with its mark. Not even the recent turns fit: the other two leave as one
    named line each, and the recent turns share the budget among themselves."""
    text = render(header, sections)
    if limit is None or len(text) <= limit:
        return text

    def items(kind):
        return [e for s in sections if s["kind"] == kind
                for e in s["entries"] if "line" not in e]

    recent, others = items("recent"), items("old") + items("tools")
    blank = {id(e): "" for s in sections for e in s["entries"] if "line" not in e}
    skeleton = len(render(header, sections, blank))
    rest = limit - skeleton - sum(len(whole(e)) for e in recent)
    if rest >= sum(_mark_len(e["total"]) for e in others):
        cut = dict(zip(map(id, others), fit(others, rest)))
        return render(header, sections, cut)
    dropped = {"old": "...[dropped: %d older turns (%d chars) over budget]",
               "tools": "...[dropped: %d tool texts (%d chars) over budget]"}
    kept = []
    for s in sections:
        gone = [e for e in s["entries"] if "line" not in e]
        if s["kind"] not in dropped or not gone:
            kept.append(s)
            continue
        lines = [e for e in s["entries"] if "line" in e]
        lines.append({"line": dropped[s["kind"]]
                      % (len(gone), sum(e["total"] for e in gone))})
        kept.append(dict(s, entries=lines))
    blank = {id(e): "" for e in recent}
    skeleton = len(render(header, kept, blank))
    cut = dict(zip(map(id, recent), fit(recent, limit - skeleton)))
    return render(header, kept, cut)


def read_back(text):
    """A prompt this cell wrote, back in its header and sections -- the one
    document a refusal hands back. None when it is not one."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    header, sections, cur = [], [], None
    for n, line in enumerate(lines):
        nxt = lines[n + 1] if n + 1 < len(lines) else None
        title = (TITLE_OLD.match(line) and "old") or (line == TITLE_RECENT and "recent") \
            or (line == TITLE_TOOLS and "tools")
        if title and (cur is None or lines[n - 1] == ""):
            cur = {"title": line, "kind": title, "entries": []}
            sections.append(cur)
            continue
        if line == "" and nxt is not None and (TITLE_OLD.match(nxt) or nxt in (TITLE_RECENT, TITLE_TOOLS)) \
                and cur is not None:
            continue  # the blank line between two sections
        if cur is None:
            header.append(line)
            continue
        lead = TOOL_LEAD if cur["kind"] == "tools" else TURN_LEAD
        m = lead.match(line)
        if m:
            cur["entries"].append(item(m.group(0), line[m.end():]))
        elif line.startswith("...[dropped: ") or line == NO_TURNS or not cur["entries"] \
                or "line" in cur["entries"][-1]:
            cur["entries"].append({"line": line})
        else:
            last = cur["entries"][-1]
            last.update(item(last["lead"], whole(last) + "\n" + line))
    if not sections:
        return None
    return header, sections

# The prompt lives HERE, in the glue phase -- an llm cell has no params.system
# slot (P15 lesson); its system state arrives by message, and this hive sends
# it fresh with every batch (accumulate-replace per path, so re-sending is an
# idempotent upsert).
INSTRUCTIONS = (
    "You are the session summarizer of an agent. A conversation generation "
    "has closed; write the handover summary its successor wakes up with, so "
    "the transition is not noticeable.\n"
    "Weight by recency: the recent turns deserve the most detail, older "
    "turns fade to their essentials. Always keep hard facts - names, dates, "
    "numbers, decisions, preferences, open tasks - even from the oldest "
    "turns.\n"
    "Write plain prose, no headings. Do not address the user; describe the "
    "session. An empty or short session yields a short, honest summary - "
    "never invent content the session does not contain.")

doc = _doc
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
session = str(hop.get("session_id", "") or ctx.get("session_id", "") or "default")


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def role_of(t):
    return "user" if t.get("origin") == "user" else "assistant"


def llm_call(text, turns, refit=False):
    header = {"route": "llm", "session_id": session, "turn_count": str(turns)}
    if refit:
        header["window_refit"] = "1"
    emit([{"header": header,
           "system": {"instructions": {"text": INSTRUCTIONS}},
           "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": text}]}])


if lane == "in_batch":
    # The collector's close batch (R-OS-6): messages[] the whole day in order,
    # the raw round rows in the top-level slot `rounds`. One batch, one prompt.
    msgs = [m for m in d.get("messages", []) if isinstance(m, dict)]
    recent = msgs[-RECENT_TURNS:] if RECENT_TURNS > 0 else []
    older = msgs[:len(msgs) - len(recent)]
    # Tool rounds as context. The leg-* rows are the collector's bookkeeping
    # (assembly legs, eviction reports) and carry no session content of their
    # own -- the turns above already are the conversation.
    tools = []
    for r in d.get("rounds", []) or []:
        if not isinstance(r, dict) or r.get("role") not in ("assistant", "tool"):
            continue
        t = r.get("turn")
        entries = t if isinstance(t, list) else ([t] if isinstance(t, dict) else [])
        for x in entries:
            if not isinstance(x, dict):
                continue
            kind = x.get("type")
            if kind not in ("tool_call", "tool_result"):
                continue
            word = "call" if kind == "tool_call" else "result"
            tools.append(("- iter %s %s %s: " % (r.get("iter", 0), word, x.get("id", "")),
                          str(x.get("text", "") or "")))
    dropped_tools = tools[:-ROUND_LINES] if ROUND_LINES > 0 else list(tools)
    tools = tools[-ROUND_LINES:] if ROUND_LINES > 0 else []

    def turn_item(t):
        return {"lead": "- %s: " % role_of(t), "head": str(t.get("text", "") or ""),
                "total": len(str(t.get("text", "") or ""))}

    header = ["Session %s closed with %d turns." % (session, len(msgs)), ""]
    sections = []
    if older:
        sections.append({"title": "## %d older turns (oldest first)" % len(older),
                         "kind": "old", "entries": [turn_item(t) for t in older]})
    sections.append({"title": TITLE_RECENT, "kind": "recent",
                     "entries": [turn_item(t) for t in recent] or [{"line": NO_TURNS}]})
    if tools or dropped_tools:
        lines = []
        if dropped_tools:
            lines.append({"line": "...[dropped: %d older tool lines (%d chars) over round_lines]"
                          % (len(dropped_tools), sum(len(x[1]) for x in dropped_tools))})
        lines += [{"lead": head, "head": text, "total": len(text)} for head, text in tools]
        sections.append({"title": TITLE_TOOLS, "kind": "tools", "entries": lines})
    llm_call(shape(header, sections, budget_chars(asked_soft(ctx), PROMPT_SHARE)), len(msgs))

if lane == "in_answer":
    text = ""
    for m in d.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("origin") == "assistant" and m.get("type") in ("text", None):
            text = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
    if not text.strip():
        # system.* is accumulate-replace per path: an empty update would
        # REPLACE a real handover with nothing. Rather no update, loud lane.
        emit([{"header": {"route": "summary_error", "session_id": session,
                          "error_code": "empty_summary"},
               "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                             "text": "summary failed for session %s: "
                                     "empty_summary (the writer returned no "
                                     "text)" % session}]}])
    # ONE emission, and its body IS the update: the `system.handover` upsert
    # an llm cell consumes without a provider call. No messages[] -- messages
    # would trigger an inference at the receiver.
    head = {"route": "summary", "session_id": session,
            "summary_chars": str(len(text))}
    if ctx.get("window_refit"):
        # The day went to the writer sized once more after a refusal (fix
        # review G1 M3): the summary says so, an operator sees it in the hop.
        head["window_refit"] = "1"
    emit([{"header": head, "system": {"handover": {"text": text}}}])

if lane == "in_error":
    # Degradation (GH #100 ruling): a failed call leaves on its own route
    # instead of being swallowed -- the parent tree decides (drain or alarm).
    # No retry here: retry is edge business, not template business.
    code = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "") or "unknown_error"
    # The one exception is not a retry but a measurement (GH #1085): the writer
    # refused the prompt as over its window (`input_hard`, or the window
    # itself) without calling a model, and named the number. Learn it ONCE:
    # the same day, read back from the refused prompt, at half of that number.
    # A second refusal (context `window_refit`) leaves like any other error.
    err = ((d.get("meta") or {}).get("error") or {}) if isinstance(d.get("meta"), dict) else {}
    bound = err.get("input_hard") or err.get("context_window")
    refused = [m for m in d.get("messages", []) or []
               if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("origin") == "user"]
    if (code == "invalid_input" and err.get("kind") in ("input_over_hard", "input_over_window")
            and budget_chars(bound, 1.0) is not None and not ctx.get("window_refit")
            and refused):
        text = str(refused[-1].get("text", "") or "")
        limit = budget_chars(bound, PROMPT_SHARE)
        doc_ = read_back(text)
        smaller = shape(doc_[0], doc_[1], limit) if doc_ else clip(text, limit, CUT_HINT)
        m = re.match(r"Session .* closed with (\d+) turns\.", text)
        if len(smaller) < len(text):
            sys.stderr.write("summarizer prep: writer refused over its window "
                             "(%s tokens) -- the day sized once more at half "
                             "of it\n" % bound)
            llm_call(smaller, m.group(1) if m else "", refit=True)
    emit([{"header": {"route": "summary_error", "session_id": session,
                      "error_code": code},
           "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                         "text": "summary failed for session %s: %s"
                                 % (session, code)}]}])

# Terminal by design: an unknown lane parks, it does not guess.
emit([])

recent_turns.description: How many of the newest turns of the closed session travel VERBATIM into the summarizer prompt. Everything before them phases out. A param of this cell since summarizer@2.1.0 rather than an environment token (GH #138), so two summarizers in one colony can weight their days apart.

round_lines.description: How many tool-activity lines enter the prompt at most; the newest are kept and the dropped ones are named in the prompt (count and characters). A param since summarizer@2.1.0 (GH #138).

input_soft_fallback.description: The window of `./writer` in tokens (GH #1085, R-IG-1; a request's `input_soft` is the asker's window and is not read): `input_soft` of the catalog row `input_soft_fallback_row` names, the model the writer is born on (OR-IG-9). That model is a birth token (`ctx.model`), and the llm-registry's tier for it is `light`, `openai/gpt-6-luna`. The prompt takes half of it, at three characters a token. A writer started on a model of its own with a smaller window refuses a longer prompt as over its `input_hard`, and the day is sized once more at half of that number. 0: no window, the day travels whole.

input_soft_fallback_row.description: The catalogue row (`model_id` in `llm-registry/store/seed/models.jsonl`) whose `input_soft` `input_soft_fallback` is: the model `./writer` is born on -- a birth token (`ctx.model`) whose llm-registry tier for a small, inexpensive writer is `light` (OR-IG-9, GH #1085). A label for the reader and for the drift lock `gh1085_fallback_windows_match_the_catalog`, which holds the two together; the script does not read it. A receiver born on another model sets both.

description.purpose: The glue half of the summarizer: shapes a closed session's write batch into ONE recency-weighted prompt for the writer llm (recent turns verbatim, older turns and tool rounds whole up to half of the writer's window -- the request's `input_soft`, else `input_soft_fallback` -- and beyond it cut fairly with a mark that names what was shown of how much), and forms the writer's answer into ONE system.handover update - the fresh memory the next generation wakes up with. The prompt lives here, in the glue phase, because an llm cell has no params.system slot; the instructions ride as a system update next to the prompt document.
description.use_when: Inside the summarizer hive, behind the collector's write batch. The parent edge names the entry lane (hop.route == 'write' -> set_hop 'in_batch').
description.not_in_scope: No inference (the writer llm answers). No judgement about what the day was worth - the weighting is deterministic structure, the judgement is the model's prose. No retry on failure: retry is edge business; a failed call leaves on summary_error and the parent tree decides. The one second call is a measurement, not a retry: a prompt the writer refused as over its window is sized once at half of the number the refusal names (GH #1085). Not the writer of any system path outside its own two: system.instructions on the lane INTO ./writer (re-sent with every batch, accumulate-replace) and system.handover on the way out. R-OS-1 says one writer per slot; it does not say one slot per writer.
description.emits_meaning: route llm: the summarizer prompt for the writer - system.instructions the shipped prompt, messages[] one user document, hop.session_id and hop.turn_count for the internal edge to promote; hop.window_refit '1' on the one prompt sized again after a refusal, promoted to context so a second refusal leaves on summary_error. route summary: ONE emission per batch whose body is nothing but {system: {handover: {text}}} - the update an llm cell consumes without a provider call; hop.session_id and hop.summary_chars say whose and how long. route summary_error: the degradation lane - a failed or empty summary, hop.error_code the cause, one assistant text naming session and cause. An unknown lane emits nothing (empty multi-send, terminal by design).
description.consumes_meaning: Three lanes, named by hop.route: in_batch (the collector's close batch - messages[] the whole day, top-level slot rounds the raw round rows, hop.session_id/turn_count/round_count the sizes), in_answer (the writer's finished summary, session in context), in_error (the writer's error message, hop.error_code rides through; an `invalid_input` refusal with meta.error.kind `input_over_hard` or `input_over_window` hands back the refused prompt and the number, and the day is sized once more at half of it). The session is read from hop.session_id first, context.session_id second.
examples: close batch of 40 turns -> older 28 counted and whole, newest 12 verbatim, tool rounds as context -> one prompt on route llm, at most half of the writer's window (context.input_soft, else input_soft_fallback); over it the older turns and tool texts are cut fairly, each with '...[cut: <shown> of <total> chars shown; budget of the window]'
writer answers 'the user configured helix...' -> one emission on route summary with system.handover.text and summary_chars
provider 500 -> the writer's error arrives on in_error -> one emission on route summary_error with error_code provider_error

the writer refuses the prompt (invalid_input, input_over_hard, input_hard 50000) -> the same day read back from the refused prompt, sized at half of 50000 tokens -> one more prompt on route llm with hop.window_refit '1'; a second refusal leaves on summary_error
empty session -> the prompt says '0 turns' and the instructions demand a short honest summary instead of invention
